summary: Everyone except citizens of India needs a Bhutan visa, applied for online (US$40) directly or through a licensed tour operator (Bangladeshi and Maldivian citizens can also get theirs on arrival), and every visitor pays the Sustainable Development Fee — US$100 per person per night for most foreigners. Indian nationals instead obtain an entry permit and pay a lower daily fee.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date you intend to leave Bhutan. Indian nationals may instead use an original voter identity card.

travelInsurance.text: Not required. Bhutan lifted its mandatory travel insurance rule on April 23, 2024, though the Department of Tourism still strongly recommends cover for the whole trip.

currencyLimits.text: You may bring cash worth up to US$10,000. Customs rules require every passenger to declare currency above the limit set by the Royal Monetary Authority's foreign exchange regulation.

notes: You can bring a small supply of tobacco for personal use, but the UK government says you must pay taxes and duties on it and be able to show proof of payment if asked; Canada's travel advice puts the tax at 200%. Smoking is prohibited in public places.
It is illegal to take antiques out of Bhutan, and customs officials may inspect items that look like antiques (UK government).

payments.text: Australia's Smartraveller says credit cards aren't widely accepted but can be used at major hotels, that EFTPOS is available nationwide including at most hotels, and that ATMs are common in towns. The Indian rupee is also legal tender, though larger notes may not be accepted.

safety.text: Australia advises normal safety precautions in Bhutan. The crime rate is low and violent crime is rare, though petty crime such as theft, pickpocketing and bag snatching can happen. Altitude sickness is a risk above 2,500 m, and flooding and landslides can disrupt transport in the June–September monsoon.

tips.text: Budget for the Sustainable Development Fee before anything else: US$100 per person per night for most visitors (US$50 for children 6–12, free under 6), paid upfront when the visa is issued. Indian nationals pay ₹1,200 per night instead.
The UK government says you need to use tour guides when visiting places of interest, or you may be refused entry, and that permits are needed for some areas — your guide can arrange them.

Australia's Smartraveller says altitude sickness is a risk above 2,500 m, and Canada notes that several trekking trails exceed 5,000 m. Ascend slowly and make sure your insurance covers evacuation from altitude.
Dress respectfully when visiting temples and dzongs (UK government), and ask your guide before taking pictures or filming inside dzongs, temples and monasteries (Canada).

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bhutan?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you hold an Indian passport (Indian nationals need an entry permit instead). Bangladeshi and Maldivian citizens can get the visa on arrival, though applying online beforehand is recommended. Everyone else applies online at immi.gov.bt — directly or through a licensed tour operator — paying a US$40 visa fee plus the Sustainable Development Fee, and the visa is issued for your exact travel dates before arrival.

faq.question: How much is Bhutan's Sustainable Development Fee?
faq.answer: US$100 per person per night for most foreign visitors, with discounts for children (US$50 for ages 6–12, free under 6). Indian nationals pay ₹1,200 per night. The fee funds healthcare, education and conservation, and is paid before your visa or permit is issued.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Bhutan?
faq.answer: No visa, but they need an entry permit — obtainable online at immi.gov.bt or on arrival at Paro airport and the Phuentsholing land border, using a passport or voter identity card, and they pay the ₹1,200-per-night Sustainable Development Fee.

faq.question: Do I have to book a tour to visit Bhutan?
faq.answer: You can apply for the visa yourself at immi.gov.bt. But the UK government says you need to use tour guides when visiting places of interest, or you may be refused entry, and Canada's travel advice says you must buy a travel package from an authorised travel agent. Check with the Department of Immigration before planning an independent trip.

faq.question: How do I apply for a Bhutan visa?
faq.answer: Apply online at immi.gov.bt with your passport, a photo and payment of the US$40 visa fee plus the Sustainable Development Fee. Processing typically takes 3 working days once the application and fees are complete, and the visa clearance is checked at check-in for your Paro flight.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bhutan?
faq.answer: Yes — extensions are possible through the Department of Immigration portal or your operator, provided you pay the Sustainable Development Fee for the additional nights. Arrange it before your current visa period ends.
